ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the edge OA of $\triangle OABC$ is on the positive half of the x-axis, point D is on edge AB, and the extension of segment CD intersects the x-axis at point E. Lines OB and OD are connected. The inverse proportion function $y= \frac{k}{x}$ ($k>0$) passes through points B and D. If the area of $\triangle OBC$ is 4 and the area of $\triangle BDE$ is 2, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} In parallelogram $ABCD$, $CB \parallel OA$, therefore $S_{\triangle OBC} = S_{\triangle EBC} = 4$, because $S_{\triangle BDE} = 2$, therefore $S_{\triangle BDC} = S_{\triangle BDE} = 2$ therefore $CD = DE$. Because $\triangle CBD \sim \triangle EAD$, therefore $\frac{CD}{DE} = \frac{BD}{DA}$ therefore $BD = DA$, $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Draw $BM \perp OA$, $DN \perp OA$ then $MN = AN$, $DN = \frac{1}{2}BM$ because the inverse proportion function $y = \frac{k}{x}$ (k>0) passes through points $B$, $D$ therefore $S_{\triangle BOM} = S_{\triangle DON}$ therefore $OM \cdot BM = ON \cdot DN$ therefore $\frac{OM}{ON} = \frac{DN}{BM} = \frac{1}{2}$. Let $OM = t$, then $ON = 2t$, $MN = t = AN$, $OA = 3t$ therefore $OM = \frac{1}{3}OA$ therefore $S_{\triangle BOM} = \frac{1}{3}S_{\triangle BOA} = \frac{1}{3}S_{\triangle BOC} = \frac{4}{3}$. Because the inverse proportion function $y = \frac{k}{x}$ (k>0) passes through point $D$ therefore $S_{\triangle DON} = \frac{1}{2}k = \frac{4}{3}$ therefore $k = \boxed{\frac{8}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, O is located at the coordinate origin, OA is on the positive x-axis, A is between O and E, and E is a point on the right-side x-axis; B is in the first quadrant, C is in the upper left, CB is parallel to the direction of OA, and the figure OABC can be understood as a parallelogram; D is located on AB, and after the straight line CD is extended downward to the right, it intersects the x-axis at E; OB and OD are also connected in the figure, and the inverse proportional function curve y=k/x passes through B and D. Reasoning: Because CB ∥ OA, and O and E are both on the x-axis, △OBC and △EBC have BC as the same base, and the heights to BC are equal, therefore S(△EBC)=S(△OBC)=4. Also D is on CE, △EBC is divided into △BDE and △BDC, and it is known that S(△BDE)=2, so S(△BDC)=4-2=2. The bases DE and DC of △BDE and △BDC are on the same straight line CE, and they share the height from B to CE; equal areas imply DE=DC. From the parallelogram relationship CB ∥ OA, and A and E are on the x-axis, so CB ∥ EA; at the same time BD and DA are on the same straight line AB, and CD and DE are on the same straight line CE, therefore △CBD ∼ △EAD. The similarity ratio gives CD/DE=BD/DA. Since CD=DE, therefore BD=DA, and D is the midpoint of AB. Draw BM ⟂ OA and DN ⟂ OA, with feet M and N respectively. Because D is the midpoint of AB and A is on the x-axis, DN=BM/2, and N is the midpoint of AM, namely MN=AN. Both B and D are on y=k/x, so if the coordinates of B correspond to OM and BM, and the coordinates of D correspond to ON and DN, then OM·BM=ON·DN=k. Thus OM/ON=DN/BM=1/2, so ON=2OM. Let OM=t, then ON=2t, so MN=t; also MN=AN, so AN=t, hence OA=OM+MN+AN=t+t+t=3t, namely OM/OA=1/3. △BOM and △BOA have the same height BM, so S(△BOM)=(OM/OA)S(△BOA)=1/3·S(△BOA). In parallelogram OABC, △BOA and △BOC have equal areas, and S(△BOC)=4, so S(△BOA)=4, and further S(△BOM)=4/3. Since B is on the inverse proportional function y=k/x, OM·BM=k, therefore S(△BOM)=1/2·OM·BM=k/2. Thus k/2=4/3, solving gives k=8/3.

claims.claim: D is located on AB.
claims.label: perception
claims.source: D is located on AB

claims.claim: After line CD is extended downward to the right, it intersects the x-axis at E.
claims.label: perception
claims.source: After line CD is extended downward to the right, it intersects the x-axis at E

claims.claim: The inverse proportional function curve y=k/x passes through B and D.
claims.label: perception
claims.source: There is an inverse proportional function curve y=k/x passing through B and D

claims.claim: △OBC and △EBC have the same base and equal heights, so S(△EBC)=S(△OBC)=4.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: △OBC and △EBC have BC as the same base, and the heights to BC are equal, therefore S(△EBC)=S(△OBC)=4

claims.claim: From S(△EBC)=4 and S(△BDE)=2, it can be obtained that S(△BDC)=2.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Given S(△BDE)=2, so S(△BDC)=4-2=2

claims.claim: △BDE and △BDC share the height from B to CE and have equal areas, so DE=DC.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Sharing the height from B to CE, equal areas imply DE=DC

claims.claim: From the parallelogram relationship CB∥OA, and A, E are on the x-axis, it can be obtained that CB∥EA.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: From the parallelogram relationship CB ∥ OA, and A, E are on the x-axis, so CB ∥ EA

claims.claim: From CB∥EA, BD and DA being collinear, and CD and DE being collinear, it can be obtained that △CBD∼△EAD.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: BD and DA are on the same straight line AB, and CD and DE are on the same straight line CE; therefore △CBD ∼ △EAD

claims.claim: From the similarity ratio CD/DE=BD/DA and CD=DE, we can obtain BD=DA; therefore D is the midpoint of AB.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The similarity ratio gives CD/DE=BD/DA. Since CD=DE, BD=DA, and D is the midpoint of AB

claims.claim: Draw BM ⟂ OA and DN ⟂ OA, with the feet of the perpendiculars being M and N respectively.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Draw BM ⟂ OA and DN ⟂ OA, with the feet of the perpendiculars being M and N respectively

claims.claim: Because D is the midpoint of AB and A is on the x-axis, DN=BM/2.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Because D is the midpoint of AB and A is on the x-axis, DN=BM/2

claims.claim: N is the midpoint of AM, that is, MN=AN.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: And N is the midpoint of AM, that is, MN=AN

claims.claim: A point on the inverse proportional function y=k/x satisfies that the product of the abscissa and the ordinate is k.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: B and D are both on y=k/x, so if the coordinates of B correspond to OM and BM, and the coordinates of D correspond to ON and DN, then OM·BM=ON·DN=k

claims.claim: From B and D being on y=k/x, we can obtain OM·BM=ON·DN=k.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: B and D are both on y=k/x, so if the coordinates of B correspond to OM and BM, and the coordinates of D correspond to ON and DN, then OM·BM=ON·DN=k

claims.claim: Combining DN=BM/2 and OM·BM=ON·DN, we can obtain OM/ON=1/2, that is, ON=2OM.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Thus OM/ON=DN/BM=1/2, so ON=2OM

claims.claim: Let OM=t, then OA=3t, therefore OM/OA=1/3.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Let OM=t, then ON=2t, so MN=t; also MN=AN, so AN=t, and thus OA=OM+MN+AN=t+t+t=3t, that is, OM/OA=1/3

claims.claim: △BOM and △BOA have the same height BM, so S(△BOM)=(OM/OA)S(△BOA).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: △BOM and △BOA have the same height BM, therefore S(△BOM)=(OM/OA)S(△BOA)

claims.claim: In parallelogram OABC, △BOA and △BOC have equal areas, and S(△BOC)=4, so S(△BOA)=4.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: In parallelogram OABC, △BOA and △BOC have equal areas, while S(△BOC)=4, so S(△BOA)=4

claims.claim: From OM/OA=1/3 and S(△BOA)=4, we can obtain S(△BOM)=4/3.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Furthermore S(△BOM)=4/3

claims.claim: Because B is on the inverse proportional function y=k/x, S(△BOM)=1/2·OM·BM=k/2.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Since B is on the inverse proportional function y=k/x, OM·BM=k, therefore S(△BOM)=1/2·OM·BM=k/2

claims.claim: From k/2=4/3, solving gives k=8/3.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Thus k/2=4/3, solving gives k=8/3.
